chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wakes up not intending to be unjust to anyone, Allah will forgive him whatever he sins during that day, as long as he does not spill blood or consume the wealth of an orphan unlawfully.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Allah's forgiveness of daily sins according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the general forgiveness of daily minor sins to a proactive, conscious intention (niyyah) of justice, highlighting the Shia emphasis on internal disposition as the root of external action. This narration specifically excludes two major, frequently cited transgressions in the Quran—bloodshed and usurping an orphan's wealth—underscoring their severity as 'major sins' that can nullify this daily mercy. The hadith thus serves as a practical spiritual guideline for believers to maintain a state of moral readiness throughout the day.
